[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fCommunications Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The communications module contains features related to personal interactions within (and without) the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcddLetters", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3Bta1pYT8D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Letters received by the church from church people or missionaries can be added to the relevant person or missionary for archival or reference purposes.

When adding a letter to a person or missionary, note the following:
- Check the 'Is Private' checkbox if the letter is not to be displayed publicly.
    - Missionary letters will be displayed on the public 'missions' website page unless this checkbox is checked!
- If the letter should be shared with the church, check the 'Share with Church?' checkbox
    - Once the letter is shared, the 'Shared Date' field should be updated
    - The Letters To Be Shared With Church report will show all letters that should be, and have not yet been shared with the church.

Example Workflow:
1. Missionary Mike sends a prayer letter that he would like read to the church.
2. The Church Secretary receives the letter, navigates to `Missions > Missionaries > Missionary Mike > Letters to the Church` and adds the letter to the Missionary Mike document making note that the letter should be read to the church.
3. Before the next church service, the Pastor runs the `Missions > Missionary Letters` report and filters by 'Share w/ Church` to see which letters need to be read.
4. The letters are added to the `Event Schedule` for the next `Function` (Service).
5. Missionary Mike's `Missionary` document can be updated with a date to show that the letter was read to the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulHeading01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf0Bulletins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulIntro0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Bulletin is the printed handout for one function: a Letter sheet printed on both sides and folded in half. The front cover carries the church name, the function name, the date, a cover image, and a verse of the week. The inside and back hold whichever sections you switch on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulCreate001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To create a bulletin, open the function and choose 'Create -> Bulletin', or add a Bulletin and pick the function. The new bulletin starts with:
- The sections switched on in Bulletin Settings. Switch any of them off for this bulletin only; a section with nothing to print is left out automatically.
- The Missionary of the Week, picked in turn (week by week, in title order) from the missionaries whose Status is not Inactive and whose support has not ended. Change it for this bulletin if you like. Missionaries marked as sensitive are never picked, and are refused, unless 'Include Sensitive Missionaries' is on in Bulletin Settings.
- Every open prayer request that is not private. Remove the rows you do not want printed; private requests cannot be added.
- Attach a cover image, type a verse of the week, such as John 3:16, and write the welcome message and announcements.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulChurchSect1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Add a row under Sections Per Church in Bulletin Settings to give a church its own bulletin. A row replaces the whole set for that church rather than changing one part of it, so tick every section you want in it; a new row starts with the same options as the settings above. The Church Roles list is shared: it says which job titles the leadership section prints, such as Pastor or Elder. Who appears under them is always that church's own people, so each congregation's bulletin names its own pastor.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulSections1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the automatic sections print:
- Order of Worship: the function's schedule, with times and the titles of linked songs, sermons and other items.
- Church Leadership: the church roles chosen in Bulletin Settings, with the people who hold those positions on the function date.
- Upcoming: functions in the days after the function date (how many days is set in Bulletin Settings).
- Ministries: active ministries and their mission statements.
- Birthdays and Anniversaries: from the function date for the number of days set in Bulletin Settings, for active members or everyone. Names and days only; no ages or years. People with 'Hide from Directory and Bulletin' ticked on their Person record are left out, and so is a couple's anniversary when either of them is. People who have a 'Death' life event are left out too, and so is a couple's anniversary when either spouse has died.
- Church Verse: the verse set on the Church record, printed at the foot of the back cover. Like the verse of the week, it prints with its words in the church's Default Bible Translation once that translation has its text, and as the reference alone until then.
- Church Image: the image (such as a logo) set on the Church record, printed above the church name on the front cover.
- Contact Information: the church address, phone, email and website from the Church record. A branch that leaves its website blank prints its parent church's website. A blank phone or email falls back to Contact Us Settings.
- Sermon Handout Insert: when a sermon on the schedule has a Sermon Handout, a third sheet prints it twice, to cut into two half-page inserts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulPrint0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Printing: click 'Print Bulletin' and download the PDF. Print it double-sided on Letter paper, flipped on the short edge, and fold it in half. Each panel has fixed space, so shorten a section or switch one off if text is cut off. For the handout sheet, print half as many copies and cut them down the dashed line.

Portal: tick 'Show in Portal' to let signed-in members download the bulletin as a PDF from the Bulletins page of the portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X5XpRUgRXI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udda5\ufe0fPresentations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Nvk4J2JbSr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Presentations are collections of digital media slides that may be presented at a church event.
Note: there is not currently a way to actually 'present' a presentation. For more advanced use-cases we recommend FreeShow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MtTk2oxuSy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a presentation, note the following:
- Add as many slides as needed containing the content you would like to display.
- You may want to add the presentation as an item in a church event's schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fChurch Emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailIntro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Church Email sends one message to many people at once. Each person gets their own copy, so no one sees the other addresses. Only a Church Manager can send one; other staff can read the ones that were sent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailSend", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To send one:
1. Add a Church Email, or open a Group and choose 'Actions -> Send Church Email'.
2. Write the Subject and the Message. To send files with it, save it and attach them in the sidebar.
3. In 'Send To', choose who gets it:
    - Active People: everyone whose Status is Active, whatever their Membership.
    - Active Members: only the people whose Membership is Member and whose Status is Active.
    - Group: the members of one Group, whatever their Status.
4. Click 'Send Test Email' to get a copy in your own inbox.
5. Click 'Send'. Churchit tells you how many people it goes to and asks you to confirm.
To send it later, set 'Send At' before you click Send. It is sent within a few minutes of that time. Until then, 'Unschedule' turns it back into a draft.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailWho", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who gets it is worked out when it is sent, from each person's primary email, so people who joined or left since you wrote it are counted correctly. People who have a 'Death' life event, people with no email address, and anyone who unsubscribed are left out. After it is sent, 'Sent To' shows how many people it went to, and the email can no longer be changed. If it cannot be sent, it goes back to Draft and a comment on it says why.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailUnsub", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every copy has an 'Unsubscribe' link at the bottom. A person who clicks it gets no more Church Emails from your church. Members can also turn the emails off and on again on the Newsletter Subscription page in the portal. When someone without a portal login asks to get them again, open their Person and click 'Resubscribe to Church Emails'. The form shows 'Unsubscribed from Church Emails' for anyone who unsubscribed. Nothing can be sent until an outgoing Email Account is set up. With multi-church on, a Church Email goes only to the people of its own church, and only that church's groups can be picked.", "col": 12}}]
